## Details on Casting Functions {.unnumbered}


### Description

'broadcast' provides several &quot;casting&quot; functions. <br />
These can facilitate complex forms of broadcasting that would normally not be possible. <br />
But these &quot;casting&quot; functions also have their own merit, beside empowering complex broadcasting. <br />
<br />
The following casting functions are available:


<ul>
<li> [acast](acast.qmd): <br />
Casts group-based subsets of an array into a new dimension. <br />
Useful for, for example, performing <b>grouped</b> broadcasted operations.

</li>
<li> [cast_hier2dim](cast_hier2dim.qmd): <br />
Casts a nested/hierarchical list into a dimensional list (i.e. array of type <code>list</code>). <br />
Useful because one cannot broadcast through nesting, but one <b>can</b> broadcast along dimensions.

</li>
<li> [hier2dim](hier2dim.qmd), [hiernames2dimnames](hier2dim.qmd): <br />
Helper functions for [cast_hier2dim](cast_hier2dim.qmd).

</li>
<li> [cast_dim2hier](cast_dim2hier.qmd): <br />
Casts a dimensional list into a nested/hierarchical list; the opposite of [cast_hier2dim](cast_hier2dim.qmd).

</li>
<li> [cast_shallow2atomic](cast_shallow2atomic.qmd): <br />
Casts a (dimensional) shallow (i.e. non-nested) list into an atomic vector or array. <br />
Useful because atomic vectors/arrays have access to many vectorized (broadcasted) operations that may not be available for vectors/arrays of type <code>list</code>.

</li>
<li> [cast_dim2flat](cast_dim2flat.qmd): <br />
Casts a dimensional list into a flattened list, but with names that indicate their original dimensional positions. <br />
Mostly useful for printing or summarizing dimensional lists.

</li>
<li> [dropnests](dropnests.qmd): <br />
Drop redundant nesting in lists; mostly used for facilitating the above casting functions. <br /> <br />

</li></ul>



### Shared argument <code>recurse_all</code>

The [dropnests](dropnests.qmd), [hier2dim](hier2dim.qmd), [hiernames2dimnames](hier2dim.qmd), and [cast_hier2dim](cast_hier2dim.qmd) methods
all have the <code>recurse_all</code> argument. <br />
By default <code>recurse_all = FALSE</code>,
meaning these methods do not recurse through dimensional or classed lists (like data.frames). <br />
Setting <code>recurse_all = TRUE</code>
allows these methods to recurse through all list objects,
even if they are dimensional and/or classed. <br />
<br />



### Shared Argument <code>in2out</code>

The [hier2dim](hier2dim.qmd), [hiernames2dimnames](hier2dim.qmd), [cast_hier2dim](cast_hier2dim.qmd), and [cast_dim2hier](cast_dim2hier.qmd) methods
all have the <code>in2out</code> argument. <br />
<br />
<br />
<img src="../help/figures/in2out-TRUE-green.svg" alt='[TRUE]' /> <br />
By default <code>in2out</code> is <code>TRUE</code>. <br />
This means the call <br />
<code>y &lt;- cast_hier2dim(x)</code> <br />
will cast the elements of the deepest valid depth of <code>x</code> to the rows of <code>y</code>,
and elements of the depth above that to the columns of <code>y</code>,
and so on until the surface-level elements of <code>x</code> are cast to the last dimension of <code>y</code>. <br />
<br />
Similarly, the call <br />
<code>x &lt;- cast_dim2hier(y)</code> <br />
will cast the rows of <code>y</code> to the inner most elements of <code>x</code>,
and the columns of <code>y</code> to one depth above that,
and so on until the last dimension of <code>y</code> is cast to the surface-level elements of <code>x</code>. <br />
<br />
Consider the nested list <code>x</code> with a depth of <code>3</code>,
and the recursive array <code>y</code> with 3 dimensions,
where their relationship can described as the following code: <br />
<code>y &lt;- cast_hier2dim(x)</code> <br />
<code>x &lt;- cast_dim2hier(y)</code>. <br />
Then it holds that: <br />
<code>x[[i]][[j]][[k]]</code> corresponds to <code>y[[k, j, i]]</code>, <br />
$\forall$(<code>i</code>, <code>j</code>, <code>k</code>) , provided <code>x[[i]][[j]][[k]]</code> exists. <br />
<br />
<br />
<img src="../help/figures/in2out-FALSE-red.svg" alt='[FALSE]' /> <br />
If <code>in2out = FALSE</code>, the call <br />
<code>y &lt;- cast_hier2dim(x, in2out = FALSE)</code> <br />
will cast the surface-level elements of <code>x</code> to the rows of <code>y</code>,
and elements of the depth below that to the columns of <code>y</code>,
and so on until the elements of the deepest valid depth of <code>x</code> are cast to the last dimension of <code>y</code>. <br />
<br />
Similarly, the call <br />
<code>x &lt;- cast_dim2hier(y, in2out = FALSE)</code> <br />
will cast the rows of <code>y</code> to the surface-level elements of <code>x</code>,
and the columns of <code>y</code> to one depth below that,
and so on until the last dimension of <code>y</code> is cast to the inner most elements of <code>x</code>. <br />
<br />
Consider the nested list <code>x</code> with a depth of <code>3</code>,
and the recursive array <code>y</code> with 3 dimensions,
where their relationship can described with the following code: <br />
<code>y &lt;- cast_hier2dim(x, in2out = FALSE)</code> <br />
<code>x &lt;- cast_dim2hier(y, in2out = FALSE)</code>. <br />
Then it holds that : <br />
<code>x[[i]][[j]][[k]]</code> corresponds to <code>y[[i, j, k]]</code>, <br />
$\forall$(<code>i</code>, <code>j</code>, <code>k</code>) , provided <code>x[[i]][[j]][[k]]</code> exists. <br /> <br />



### Examples
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=TRUE, collapse = TRUE, comment = NA}
library("broadcast")


# recurse_all demonstration ====
x <- list(
  a = list(list(list(list(1:10)))),
  b = data.frame(month.abb, month.name),
  c = data.frame(month.abb),
  d = array(list(1), c(1,1,1))
)

dropnests(x) # by default, recurse_all = FALSE

dropnests(x, recurse_all = TRUE) # recurse_all = TRUE



# in2out demonstration ====
x <- list(
  group1 = list(
    class1 = list(
      height = rnorm(10, 170),
      weight = rnorm(10, 80),
      sex = sample(c("M", "F", NA), 10, TRUE)
    ),
    class2 = list(
      height = rnorm(10, 170),
      weight = rnorm(10, 80),
      sex = sample(c("M", "F", NA), 10, TRUE)
    )
  ),
  group2 = list(
    class1 = list(
      height = rnorm(10, 170),
      weight = rnorm(10, 80),
      sex = sample(c("M", "F", NA), 10, TRUE)
    ),
    class2 = list(
      height = rnorm(10, 170),
      weight = rnorm(10, 80),
      sex = sample(c("M", "F", NA), 10, TRUE)
    )
  )
)

# in2out = TRUE (default):
x2 <- cast_hier2dim(x)
dimnames(x2) <- hiernames2dimnames(x)
print(x2)
cast_dim2flat(x2[1,1,,drop = FALSE])

# in2out = FALSE:
x2 <- cast_hier2dim(x, in2out = FALSE)
dimnames(x2) <- hiernames2dimnames(x, in2out = FALSE)
print(x2)
cast_dim2flat(x2[1,1,,drop = FALSE])



```
